title: Bombay High Court Quashes Rs 329 Crore Reassessment Against Grasim Over Vodafone Idea Rights Shares
case_name: Grasim Industries Limited v. Deputy Commissioner of Income-tax & Ors.
citation: Writ Petition No. 4298 of 2026; 2026 LLBiz HC(BOM) 591
card_summary: A division bench led by Justice B.P. Colabawalla quashed a Section 148 reassessment notice against Grasim Industries over its subscription to Vodafone Idea's rights issue. The department had treated the gap between the subscription price and a higher valuation as a taxable benefit of about Rs 329 crore under Section 56(2)(x). The court held rights allotment is not automatically taxable on a mere price difference.
card_tip: A rights issue taken up in proportion to existing shareholding, where the shareholder's percentage stake stays unchanged, is not automatically caught by Section 56(2)(x) just on a higher valuation.
verification_notes: LiveLawBiz, Business Upturn and Kalkine agree on the 22 October 2026 date, the Rs 329 crore figure tied to the Vodafone Idea rights issue, the Section 56(2)(x) and Section 148 grounds, and that the ruling is confined to facts where the petitioner's shareholding percentage was unchanged. Bench composition is reported consistently as led by Colabawalla J.; the second judge's name was not confirmed identically across sources, so it is omitted here pending the certified order. Grasim's own exchange clarification (25 October 2026) is noted but not treated as an independent source.
